transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-11-09 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~38 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramos (Head of AI, Orchid), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Nadia Gomez (Data Scientist)

Summary (auto): quick intro, qualification, PLG quickstart flow details, security questions, wrap + next steps.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, this is Arjun, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:08 Speaker 2 (Sofia): Good, thanks. Excited to learn more. We sent over a calendar note, hope that's okay.
00:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yep perfect. Quick agenda, we'll ask a few qualification questions, run through the PLG quickstart experience, talk about when Dedicated/Private might make sense, and then agree next steps. Sound good?
00:22 Speaker 3 (Arjun): Hi all. I'll jump in on the technical bits — latency profiles, safety, and quick benchmark ideas.
00:29 Speaker 2 (Sofia): Great. Quick intro from our side: I'm Sofia, Head of AI at Orchid Health, we build a clinical search/product that surfaces relevant notes and patient history. Liam runs infra and Nadia does the modeling.
00:42 Speaker 4 (Liam): Hey. Our immediate constraint is PHI — we need to keep a lot of data on-prem, but for initial experiments we're open to hosted with data minimization. Timeline is quick: POC in 3-4 weeks.
00:55 Speaker 5 (Nadia): We currently use a mix of in-house embeddings and OpenAI for generation, but cost is creeping up and latency can be variable.
01:05 Speaker 3 (Arjun): Understood. For PLG quickstart we typically give free credits to get you to first-token quickly — sign up, redeem credits, run a short script we provide and you're generating within an hour, often minutes.
01:20 Speaker 2 (Sofia): Nice. How locked in is the hosted route? If we like results, can we later move to Dedicated or Private without significant code changes?
01:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, that's one of the things customers like — same Redwood API across hosted, Dedicated, and Private. You can pin model versions and rollout policies; the SDK calls don't change. There may be config or network changes for Private.
01:44 Speaker 4 (Liam): On Private, we need to know about KMS/HSM support and audit logs. Also SSO — we use Okta.
01:53 Speaker 3 (Arjun): We support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated, and our control plane integrates with SAML/Okta; audit logs are available with extended retention add-on. We'll share the SOC 2 report and a network architecture doc after this call.
02:10 Speaker 5 (Nadia): For embeddings, we're sensitive to both throughput and unit cost. Do you have batching/caching recommendations?
02:19 Speaker 3 (Arjun): Yup — Redwood has intelligent batching and prefix/KV cache — sorry sometimes the transcription says K V cash — the runtime does automatic batching and we can tune minibatch sizes. For embeddings we also suggest caching vectors for frequent queries.
02:36 Speaker 2 (Sofia): How long until we can run a benchmark? We want to measure tokens/sec and median latency for gen and embeddings.
02:45 Speaker 1 (Maya): We can get you started today with credits; Arjun can prepare a small benchmark script (curl + Python sample) that runs both embeddings and a generation workload. Expect ~30–60 minutes to set up and then the run itself depends on sample size.
02:59 Speaker 4 (Liam): For compliance we might need to run in a VPC. Can the hosted API call back to a VPC endpoint or do we need Dedicated?
03:09 Speaker 3 (Arjun): Hosted can't be deployed into your VPC, but we support network peering or PrivateLink for enterprise customers; most customers who need strict network isolation choose Dedicated or Private deployments. Hosted is great for quick iteration.
03:24 Speaker 2 (Sofia): What's the typical cost delta between hosted and Dedicated? We care about unit cost for embeddings primarily.
03:31 Speaker 1 (Maya): It varies — Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale compared to hosted volume pricing, because you reserve GPU capacity. For initial POC hosted is usually fine; if you see high steady throughput we can run a capacity estimate.
03:46 Speaker 5 (Nadia): Any gotchas around prompt engineering when switching model variants? Like, will prompts need changing if we switch quantized model for cost reasons?
03:55 Speaker 3 (Arjun): Sometimes small prompt tweaks can help with quantized models. Redwood Optimize provides recommended quantization and prompts per workload; for the quickstart we'll use a reference model in our catalog and note any differences.
04:10 Speaker 2 (Sofia): We also asked about data retention and access controls — are customer logs accessible to Redwood staff?
04:19 Speaker 3 (Arjun): By default we retain logs for X days for debugging, but for Dedicated/Private you can disable or route logs to your S3 and we can restrict Redwood access; we'll share the specifics in the security packet.
04:33 Speaker 4 (Liam): Good. On the onboarding front, what's time-to-first-token if we self-serve?
04:39 Speaker 1 (Maya): Typical is under 30 minutes if you already have an account and Okta SSO, longer if you need SAML setup; with the quickstart guide and sample code it's often minutes.
04:50 Speaker 2 (Sofia): Do you provide client SDKs? We prefer node/python.
04:54 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes—official SDKs for Python, Node, and Go; CLI too. We'll share a one-line curl example which is usually easiest for the POC.
05:04 Speaker 5 (Nadia): For model catalog, can we bring our own fine-tuned model or do we only use Redwood-hosted models?
05:12 Speaker 3 (Arjun): For Private you can bring models; Dedicated can support customer-run weights in certain enterprise setups. Hosted currently uses curated models from the catalog but we also support model upload for partners — we can discuss with Solutions Architecture if that's a long-term requirement.
05:27 Speaker 2 (Sofia): How do you handle fallback if a model is temporarily overloaded? We need reliability for demo.
05:33 Speaker 3 (Arjun): Smart routing — requests can fall back to a compatible variant or region, and you can configure priority tiers. For PLG quickstarts we recommend building a simple retry/waitbackoff logic; we can demo automatic fallback policies in the Console.
05:48 Speaker 4 (Liam): Ok. Any regulatory certifications? SOC2 was mentioned, any PCI/PHI support?
05:56 Speaker 3 (Arjun): SOC2 Type II available; for PHI you'd likely need Private or a well-structured Dedicated deployment with BAAs — we can share legal/IT guidance. PCI typically not relevant unless you're processing payment data.
06:10 Speaker 2 (Sofia): On the quickstart credits, are they tied to specific models or usable across the catalog?
06:16 Speaker 1 (Maya): Credits are generally usable across the Redwood catalog for hosted API use; for Dedicated/Private a different commercial model applies. We'll include the redemption link and instructions.
06:26 Speaker 5 (Nadia): For embeddings, do you return vector dims and do you support cosine dot product in Redwood or expected to do in our infra?
06:33 Speaker 3 (Arjun): We return vector arrays; Redwood doesn't currently offer a managed vector DB — you compute similarity in your stack. Some partners integrate with vector stores — we can share examples.
06:46 Speaker 2 (Sofia): That works. Next, can you walk through a short demo of the quickstart CLI flow?
06:52 Speaker 1 (Maya): Sure, Arjun do you want to screen-share? (small pause) — okay, I'll describe — first you sign up at app.redwood.ai, verify email, then under Quickstart you click Redeem Credits and copy an API key. Then pip install redwood and run a one-liner. Example: `redwood gen --model redwood-mini --prompt "summarize clinical note"` — response streams back.
07:19 Speaker 3 (Arjun): The CLI uses the same API so you can switch to SDK with the same key. For local benchmarking we usually recommend our small harness: a python script that hits the embed endpoint with batch sizes 1, 8, 32 to see throughput/latency curves.
07:35 Speaker 4 (Liam): Can we run a benchmark that approximates our infra? We have long clinical notes, 1–2k tokens on average.
07:42 Speaker 3 (Arjun): Yes, please share a small sample and we'll run a benchmark using similar seq len; the runtime chooses kernels based on seq length distribution and we can show performance variance.
07:52 Speaker 2 (Sofia): Anything else on security we should know before handing over sample data?
07:56 Speaker 3 (Arjun): Avoid PHI in the hosted POC if you're not comfortable. If you need to include PHI we recommend Dedicated/Private and a signed BAA — we'll route that to Legal. For the initial run, you can anonymize or use synthetic data.
08:14 Speaker 5 (Nadia): On the topic of model quality monitoring, do you have built-in evals?
08:20 Speaker 3 (Arjun): Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets and evals; we can enable trial evaluation metrics for the POC.
08:33 Speaker 2 (Sofia): Great. Budget question: if this POC looks good, what's the pilot pricing model?
08:39 Speaker 1 (Maya): For pilots we usually offer continued hosted credits and then a time-limited Dedicated proposal if you want reserved capacity; we'll draft a pilot proposal after the benchmark.
08:49 Speaker 4 (Liam): One practical: our internal security team will likely want to run static scans on any SDKs; are the SDKs open-source?
08:56 Speaker 3 (Arjun): Yes, SDKs are OSS on GitHub; you can scan them. We'll include links.
09:03 Speaker 2 (Sofia): Okay let's recap and agree next steps.
09:06 Speaker 1 (Maya): Recap: we'll send the quickstart guide and redeem link, Arjun will send a small benchmark harness and example prompts, and Orchid will share a sample anonymized dataset and success metrics. We'll also share SOC2 + network diagram. Schedule: aim to run benchmark next week, sync after with results.
09:28 Speaker 4 (Liam): Sounds good. Any blockers on our side? We need legal to approve any PHI handling for Dedicated.
09:35 Speaker 1 (Maya): Noted. We'll mark that as an item and include contacts for legal/BAA discussions.
09:41 Speaker 2 (Sofia): Thanks, this was helpful. One last thing — how do you track cost per embedding? We want simple reporting to show cost savings versus current vendor.
09:52 Speaker 3 (Arjun): In Console you get token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards; we can export usage CSVs to plug into your finance models.
10:04 Speaker 2 (Sofia): Perfect. We'll wait for the emails and run the POC.
10:08 Speaker 1 (Maya): Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links and docs later today. Appreciate your time.

(End of recording)
